note: P0 (live, player report — Paione): 'when training combat, Strength/Defense/HP exp is not saving; only Attack saves'. supabase/functions/hr-accrue/accrual.js settled every combat window with resolveStyle(eq.weaponType, null) — null makes resolveStyle fall to the FIRST key of the weapon family, sword.accurate, which routes 100% of styled XP to ATTACK — because the player's chosen style had no server home: it lived in the save blob, then in the client_state RESIDUE bag, which is self-only and which the server is forbidden to read for authority. Skills are server-of-record and ARMED, so each settle retired the client's predicted Strength/Defence XP and wrote the Attack-only answer instead. Adds player_state.combat_style jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}' (the per-weapon-family choice map, e.g. {"sword":"defensive"}; a PARTIAL map is normal and {} means 'chosen nothing', never 'chose Accurate') with a jsonb_typeof='object' check; public.hr_combat_styles (family, style_key, is_default) seeded from src/core/styles.js COMBAT_STYLES/DEFAULT_STYLE_KEYS and bound to it in BOTH directions by tests/combat-style.mjs, carrying NOT ONE simulation number (accuracyMod/damageMod/speedMod/xp ratios stay in the one module the picker, the router and the engine all import); and hr_set_style__ungated + the rate-gated hr_set_style wrapper (authenticated-only; the inner AND hr_engine are shut out — the accrual engine reads the style and must never be able to choose which skill it pays). The caller sends a FAMILY and a KEY and nothing else, both looked up in the server catalogue; an unknown pair is REFUSED (unknown_family / unknown_style), never clamped, because a clamp would silently route XP somewhere the player did not choose — this file's own bug in miniature. Takes the SAME per-character advisory lock hr_apply takes, MERGES one key (a call about swords never resets the bow), bumps version (the column PRICES an absence — XP routing and, through speedMod, the swing interval — so an in-flight accrual must be made to re-read), and refuses mid-absence with collect_first rather than stamping accrued_to, which would confiscate the unpaid window (the hr_set_auto_eat ruling; the 60s grace mirrors ACCRUE_MIN_MS). p_idem caches the SUCCESS envelope in player_intents, read INSIDE the lock; refusals are deliberately NOT cached so a collect_first becomes retryable the moment the settle lands. It writes NO player_ledger row: the bucket is 30/min (a style flip is free and harmless by construction) and a per-gesture journal at that rate is the per-tick logging journal rule 6 forbids — if an audit trail is ever wanted, DROP THE BUCKET TO 30/HOUR FIRST. Patches hr_rpc_gate (bucket hr_set_style, 30/min — an unknown bucket fails CLOSED, so without it every call would 429) and hr_state_of (one key, 'combat_style', INSIDE the `state` object next to tool_carry/fight, because the accrual shell reads it off the row as st.combat_style) PROGRAMMATICALLY at guarded exactly-once anchors, so it carries no literal create-or-replace header for either and is a member of NO derivation chain and takes over no last-toucher role. MUST run AFTER 2026-08-26-marks-record.sql (the last STATIC hr_state_of toucher, whose 'streak_day_key' terminator is the anchor) and after every later programmatic hr_state_of patcher (bank-store, client-state, trait-buy) and after the current hr_rpc_gate last toucher (2026-08-23-trait-buy.sql). ⚠ REQUIRES AN EDGE REDEPLOY: supabase/functions/hr-accrue/accrual.js, index.ts and set-activity.js all change, and the migration alone leaves the engine still reading null. The column's PRESENCE is the switch (st.combat_style ?? null degrades to exactly the pre-migration behaviour), so the two halves are safe in either order. Reversibility: additive — drop the two functions and hr_combat_styles, optionally drop the column, and re-apply the previous hr_state_of/hr_rpc_gate last-toucher; reverting restores the bug and corrupts nothing. §8 PROVES on apply, in an HR819-rolled-back subtransaction: a fresh character projects {} (not a pre-filled default); an unknown family, an unknown style and a CROSS-FAMILY key are each refused by name and write nothing; the happy path stores the map, bumps version and reaches the envelope; a second family MERGES rather than replaces; a replay on the same idem returns the original envelope with no second version bump; a mid-absence flip is refused collect_first, writes nothing and is NOT cached; the SAME key then succeeds once the window is paid; and a second FRESH character is unaffected (the control).
